input.question: Why didn't we actively re-center the ranges to follow the price (frequent narrowing), instead of staying wide?
input.reference: On 720 days 0 of 21 narrow configurations passed the gate, and the one live narrowing (31.08 to 11.09) ended -$32 vs HODL, so on 16.09 narrowing was rejected again because the upside (about +$1 per episode) is far smaller than the loss when the price leaves a ±5% range (about -$30).
input.answer: The project chose wide passive ranges because backtests showed frequent narrowing/re-centering destroyed value. Narrow ranges earned 4x more fees but lost more to impermanent loss (IL) and swap costs from re-centering. Specifically, "zwężanie zarobiło DUŻO więcej fee... a skończyło NIŻEJ" because "IL i re-centering zjadły ~$1.9k... ponad to, co dołożyły fee". In the 720-day walkforward, passive wide beat narrow in 63-60% of windows, and even in flat regimes where narrowing theoretically has an edge, passive wide won (86% vs 59% on cbBTC). The mechanism is described as "short gamma": every re-centering "REALIZUJE dywergencję" (realizes the divergence/loss).

quotes.quote: zwężanie zarobiło DUŻO więcej fee — cbBTC $2169 vs $541, base-030 $3147 vs $1354 — a skończyło NIŻEJ.
Czyli IL i re-centering zjadły ~$1.9k (cbBTC) i ~$2.9k (base-030) ponad to, co dołożyły fee
Wąskie pasmo to short gamma: każde przejście postury REALIZUJE dywergencję.
Pasywny szeroki bije FlatOnly ±5% wszędzie — %wygr. 63 vs 43 (cbBTC) i 60 vs 45–47 (base-030)

verdict.correctnessReason: The answer rightly says narrowing lost value overall, but it misses the reference's key points: 0 of 21 narrow configurations passed the gate, the live narrowing ended -$32 vs HODL, and the 16.09 rejection rested on a ~+$1 upside versus a ~-$30 downside.
verdict.faithfulnessReason: The fee/IL figures, the short-gamma mechanism and the 63/60% win rates are quoted, but the flat-regime 86% vs 59% figure, the 720-day label and the blanket '4x more fees' (base-030 is only about 2.3x) are not backed by the quotes.

input.question: Why did we keep the capital commitment small even though ETH and BTC were rising?
input.reference: Tranche 1 ($6 092) was planned as a first stage and run as an operational experiment on a calibration the team itself considered broken (720 d: 0/21), the entry after an ETH +25%/90d pump was recorded with an explicit FOMO note, and on 02.09 the product failed to beat HODL in all five measurements, so the planned scale-up never happened.
input.answer: The capital commitment was kept small because the analysis showed no alpha: the product is essentially HODL plus yield minus drag. Specifically, in a rising market the strategy earns less than HODL because the pool sells the rising asset (the 'sufit pasma' or band ceiling limits upside capture), while in a crash it loses significantly more. The team concluded the durable value was in measurement and the research machine, not in scaling up capital for returns.

input.question: Why did the bot never open, close or re-range positions on its own, and was automatic execution possible at all?
input.reference: The bot ran in PROPOSE mode with no wallet key on the server, so the owner signed every transaction; the only cost was signing delay (up to ~13 h at night, ~61 h over a weekend), measured from day one, and AUTO existed only as a later rung of the trust path OBSERVE-PROPOSE-AUTO that was deliberately not enabled at the start.
input.answer: The bot never opened, closed, or re-ranged positions automatically because the system was deliberately kept in PROPOSE mode. As documented, "Everything runs in PROPOSE mode: the bot executes nothing on its own." This meant that any action—opening, rebalancing, or closing a position—was generated as a proposal requiring manual approval and signature in a browser wallet (Rabby). While the architecture defined an "AUTO" mode for "execution within limits," this feature was "not built" and "never enabled." Consequently, automatic execution was not possible; the bot could only monitor, calculate signals, and prepare transactions for the owner to sign.

Wide passive ranges earned fewer fees but outperformed HODL in flat windows. The project attributes up-window losses to "LVR (Loss-Versus-Rebalancing)" and "realized IL," not to lower fee accrual.

input.question: What infrastructure problems were there, was anything changed on the production machine while the capital was already invested, and when?
input.reference: Before the capital (27.08) there was the .bot/pipeline overwrite incident (17.08), the auto-pull runner withdrawn (18.08) and the NSSM to pm2 migration rolled back (21.08); while the capital was in the LP (27.08 to 18.09) the Windows machine was changed repeatedly: bot and UI deployments with restarts on 28.08, 29.08 (including sigma on the 15-minute grid), 31.08, 01.09, 02.09, 03.09 and 11.09, plus a disk replacement on the night of 02/03.09 that stopped the pipeline, report and observer; known ledger bugs (anchor chain, cost after the 11.09 rebalance) were left unfixed.
input.answer: Yes. On 21 Aug 2026, a deploy script (`deploy/deploy.ps1`) that predated the 10 Aug migration still ended with `pm2 startOrReload` + `pm2 save`, while production used NSSM services. A session stopped the NSSM services and started pm2, leaving the production bot on pm2. This caused recurring visible terminal windows after reboots and risked two bot instances running simultaneously. The script was rewritten for NSSM the same day. Additionally, on 31 Aug, a rebalance transaction reverted due to a stale pool state in the UI, fixed the same day.

input.question: Is FLAT_NARROW a specific position or some kind of range algorithm?
input.reference: Neither: it is a proposal type (kind) emitted by the bot's flat detector when the flat regime is confirmed (|gap to the EMA| < 2% for at least 12 h), proposing to narrow an existing wide position to a fixed ±5%, with FLAT_WIDEN as the opposite card when |gap| > 5%; unsigned cards expire on a TTL and come back.
input.answer: FLAT_NARROW is a specific proposal kind (a concrete action), not a range algorithm. It is the bot's proposal to narrow an existing position's range to a fixed product width (e.g., ±5%) once a flat state is confirmed. The actual range calculation uses a separate function, `suggestFixedRange`, driven by a product width parameter (`productNarrowWidthPct`), not a dynamic algorithm like k×σ. The proposal itself carries the computed `suggestedRange`, `costUsd`, and `paybackDays` for a specific pool.

input.question: What does the function fetchFreshPool do?
input.reference: It re-reads the pool state on-chain (factory.getPool, then slot0 and liquidity) right before the mint step of a rebalance or rotation, so the new position is built from the current price instead of the price captured when the modal opened, and falls back to the old pool if the lookup fails; it was added after the 11.09 widening failed once on 'Price slippage check' and was never exercised live, since the only later chance (a FLAT_NARROW card on 16.09) was not signed and the positions were closed by hand in Uniswap.
input.answer: fetchFreshPool (in src/utils/uniswap.ts) fetches the current on-chain state of a Uniswap v3 pool: it calls factory.getPool, then reads slot0 and liquidity, and constructs a new Pool object with the same tokens and fee tier. It is fail-open, returning the old pool if the factory or RPC call fails. It is wired into useRebalanceExecution and useRotateExecution right before buildMintStep, so rebalance/rotate steps use fresh price data rather than a stale cached pool.
